entries.title: Bears WR Luther Burden leaves practice early with injury
entries.summary: <p>Bears receiver Luther Burden limped off the field with an athletic trainer about 45 minutes into Saturday morning’s practice at Halas Hall.</p><p>Burden and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson landed awkwardly during the last one-on-one rep in the end zone.</p><p>Stevenson spent a minute stretching out his hip and groin area but stayed in practice. Burden took a knee before walking around for a minute and eventually leaving the field.</p><p>Burden, a second-round pick last year, has been a popular breakout candidate both inside and outside Halas Hall this year. Coach Ben Johnson famously said he'd buy stock in the receiver's career.</p><p>The Bears practiced without left tackle Braxton Jones and defensive end Montez Sweat. The two were hurt Thursday but a source said they likely avoided any long-term damage .</p><p>The Bears practice again Sunday and are set to scrimmage Tuesday. They'll hold a walk-through at Stevenson High School on Monday.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: 3 shot, 1 fatally, in Englewood
entries.summary: <p>A man was killed and two others were injured in a shooting Friday night in Englewood on the South Side.</p><p>Three men were standing outside in the 700 block of West 73rd Street when they got in an argument with a person around 9:40 pm., Chicago police said. The person opened fire and struck all three men. </p><p>A 34-year-old man suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, police said. His name hasn't been released. </p><p>Another man, 50, was struck in the back and suffered a graze wound to the arm while a third man, 20, was shot in the arm. Both men drove themselves to the University of Chicago Medical Center and were in fair condition, police said. </p><p>No arrests were made. </p>

entries.title: Bears Training Camp Report, Day 9: More injuries at safety
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down the Bears’ Saturday training camp practice:</p><h3>No one’s safe(ty)</h3><p>Cam Lewis was in considerable pain at the end of practice and, after trying to stretch out his leg and hip area, was carted off the field. It was the latest injury at safety for the Bears, who lost Coby Bryant for at least two months and saw Gervarrius Owens leave on a cart Thursday. Owens was waived with an injury designation Saturday.<br>Lewis began training camp as the team’s slot cornerback because of Kyle Gordon’s calf injury but moved to safety when Bryant was hurt.</p><p>The Bears added depth Saturday, signing safety Brandon Hill and cornerback William Wright. </p><p>Lewis is the latest addition to an ever-longer injury list. Cornerbacks Terell Smith and Jaylon Jones, linebacker D’Marco Jackson, tackle Braxton Jones and defensive end Montez Sweat all sat out Saturday’s practice. Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills rotated in Jones’ place — and struggled. Rookie Malik Muhammad was solid in the slot. Neither Jones nor Sweat has a serious injury.</p><h3>Can I kick it</h3><p>After making a spectacular touchdown catch in 7-on-7 drills, tight end Colston Loveland punted the ball in celebration. That drew a flag from the referees working practice.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Best thing at <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Bears?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Bears</a> practice today; Colston Loveland punting the ball after catching a TD pass — and getting flagged. <a href="https://t.co/F7yFP5TliA">pic.twitter.com/F7yFP5TliA</a></p>— Patrick Finley (@patrickfinley) <a href="https://x.com/patrickfinley/status/2086132969081643433?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 8, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3>Sup, Coach</h3><p>NBC analyst Jason Garrett gave Bears defensive backs coach Al Harris a hug as he walked onto the practice field. Garrett was the Cowboys’ head coach from 2011-19; Harris began as a Cowboys assistant in 2020. </p><p>Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen and offensive line coach Dan Roushar, both former Saints assistants, missed practice to attend Drew Brees’ Pro Football Hall of Fame induction in Canton, Ohio.</p><h3>What’s next?</h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears practice at 12:30 p.m. Sunday at Halas Hall.<br></p>

entries.title: World Series hunger fuels Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes, who see chance to return with Cubs: ‘An addicting drug’
entries.summary: <p>KANSAS CITY – Kevin Gausman almost won a World Series ring last year.</p><p>Clay Holmes almost won a World Series ring the year before.</p><p>Almost.</p><p>For pro ballplayers, almost is usually not good enough, and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ new pair of righty pitchers – the team’s two biggest acquisitions at the trade deadline – is itching to get back to October’s ultimate stage.</p><p>“It’s an addicting drug once you get there,” Gausman said last week.</p><p>Both Gausman and Holmes, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/07/cubs-kevin-gausman-starting-pitching-jed-hoyer-mlb-trade-deadline-royals-blue-jays" >made their Cubs debuts</a> this weekend in Kansas City, had their World Series dreams stomped on by the Dodgers, who made their own massive trade-deadline splash, adding back-to-back Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in a quest for a third consecutive ring.</p><p>Team president Jed Hoyer said it’s up to the Cubs – and the rest of the sport – to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/04/cubs-dodgers-three-peat-world-series-favorites-tarik-skubal-dansby-swanson" >stop the Dodgers from accomplishing that goal</a>. He brought in these two pitchers in an effort to do just that, and even before they donned Cubs uniforms, this team showed them it might be capable of stopping a seemingly unstoppable juggernaut by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-shohei-ohtani-nl-mvp-race-dodgers-playoffs-craig-counsell-shota-imanaga" >sweeping the Dodgers at Wrigley Field</a>.</p><p>“Watching the team play [earlier this week],” Gausman said, “why wouldn’t you be excited?”</p><p>But August is different from October, and though an electric atmosphere on the North Side was certainly playoff-esque, as Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell put it, ain’t nothing like the real thing.</p><p>“I’ve been home in the offseason the last couple years, and just watching playoff baseball, you want to get in there,” righty reliever Ryan Zeferjahn, another deadline addition, said. “Hopefully, I get a taste of that this year.”</p><p>Just ask Gausman, who made two starts in last year’s World Series, only for the Dodgers to edge his Blue Jays for a championship in a seven-game classic of a Fall Classic.</p><p>“Losing was heartbreaking,” he said. “I wish every big leaguer could experience playing in the World Series, because that’s what we all dreamt of as kids. To be able to do it was so much fun, but also very heartbreaking.</p><p>“Once you’re there, all you want to do is get back. I’m really excited to, hopefully, get back there with this team.”</p><p>The Cubs woke up Saturday with the fifth best record in baseball, among the sport’s true contenders and arguably its best since June 11.</p><p>In that span, they had the second best record in the game (34-15), they led the league in runs scored (293) and OPS (.799), and their starting pitchers had a 3.22 ERA (third in MLB). Overall, they had baseball’s best defense, statistically, first in Defensive Runs Saved (79), Outs Above Average (58) and Fielding Run Value (60).</p><p>In other words, yes, the Cubs are capable of getting Gausman and Holmes back to the World Series, probably more capable now that they’re here.</p><p>The Cubs’ expectations have been at championship-or-bust level since the jump this season, and Hoyer’s work – both with big, narrative-busting offseason moves and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" >an aggressive approach at the deadline</a> – has gone hand in hand with those big dreams.</p><p>Time to get the job done.</p><p>“That’s what you play the game for. You want to win your last game,” said Holmes, who as a Yankee reliever pitched in all five games of the 2024 World Series. “You put in all the work, you put in all the preparation, you forge relationships to be a team that wins it at the end. And to know you have a real chance to do that, especially at this point in the season, is energizing.</p><p>“I’ve felt it before in my career. I’ve lost a World Series, and there’s that hunger of wanting to be the last team standing. For me, personally, to know that I have a real chance to do it here these last few months is all you can ask for.</p><p>“I feel like I’m in a great spot and just want to give everything I have, do whatever I can for this group, because it’s a special group.”</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: Bud Billiken Parade marks 97 years of tradition, bringing generations together
entries.summary: <p>As a young girl, Valerie Cadenhead remembers walking with her family to the Bud Billiken Parade.</p><p>Now, the iconic parade passes just steps from her home in Grand Boulevard, and Cadenhead’s family has continued the tradition with the next generation, marking the start of the new school year.</p><p>“It’s a tradition that we can pass down and it gives us stories to pass down,” said Cadenhead, 67, who's now a teacher herself.</p><p>Cadenhead and her family were among hundreds who gathered along Martin Luther King Drive on the South Side to watch the parade step off Saturday morning. </p><p>In its 97th year, the Bud Billiken is one of the largest and longest-running parades in the country. Founded in 1929 by Robert Sengstacke Abbott, publisher and founder of the African American newspaper the Chicago Defender, the parade was created to celebrate Black children and their achievements.</p><p>The parade features marching bands, floats, dance teams, community organizations and youth groups. The route, roughly two miles long, starts at Pershing Road and heads south down King Drive toward Washington Park, ending at Garfield Boulevard.</p><p>Gov. JB Pritzker and Mayor Brandon Johnson both were in this year's parade. The star-studded lineup also included this year’s Grand Marshal, actress LisaRaye McCoy, as well as actor Cortez Smith and comedians Cedric the Entertainer and Anthony Anderson.</p><p>This year’s parade was especially meaningful for Cadenhead, as her brother-in-law and niece took part in the festivities. Her niece was selected to join the parade’s Royal Court, an annual tradition that honors children who have demonstrated academic excellence. Meanwhile, her brother-in-law marched with the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop="">
